input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs for three years (Section 8.1) and Section 9 provides only cause-based termination rights (material breach, insolvency, security/service-level/legal/IP failures); no Customer termination for convenience exists, and Section 2.1 expressly negates any reduction or termination right against a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay commitment. Under T4C, absence of a Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation. Vendor has no convenience right today, so we preserve that by making it explicit. We insert a new Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no penalty, and overriding Section 2.1, matching the preferred position.

ops.text: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination and Customer shall owe no early-termination fee, penalty, or unaccrued or accelerated Fees, notwithstanding Section 2.1. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during an initial or renewal term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a Customer right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and no early-termination penalty, and confirmed Vendor has no mid-term walk-away right; Section 9 currently gives us only cause-based exits across a three-year term. If helpful, we can discuss 60-90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees.
proposal.summary: Insert Section 9.4 granting Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund and no Vendor convenience right.
